African Humanitarian Agency - Stronger humanitarian action in Africa

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the intervention is that the "Humanitarian Affairs Division of the African Union Commission is enabled to effectively implement the establishment and operationalisation of AfHA." This overall objective is underpinned by two outcomes, that are:
- Improving the knowledge base and strengthening the decision-making support for effective operationalization of AfHA.
- Enhance the capacity and tools for harmonization of Disaster Risk Management across Member States through AfHAs operational framework.

title.narrative: AFRICAN HUMANITARIAN AGENCY ­ STRONGER HUMANITARIAN ACTION IN AFRICA

description.narrative: During the reporting period(2025), the contribution supported continued progress toward establishing the African Humanitarian Agency (AfHA), despite delays linked to staffing gaps and institutional transitions within the African Union Commission (AUC). A key achievement was the Technical Consultation Workshop in Accra (1516 October 2025), which brought together 48 participants from Member States, RECs, AUC departments, National Societies, and partners. This workshop resulted in consensus on AfHAs operational direction, including agreement on eight priority frameworks and 18 Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). This constitutes a major step toward defining AfHAs future coordination role and has strengthened shared ownership among continental actors. As the report notes, the workshop reaffirmed coordination as AfHAs core mandate and created a unified platform for Member States and regional bodies to shape the agencys operational architecture. The contribution also enabled progress in strengthening AfHAs knowledge base. Through donor financed complementary activities, a continental mapping exercise was completed, producing a fully validated dataset covering 24 Member States, seven RECs, two AUC departments, and one specialized agency. This dataset, together with a preliminary analytical dashboard, provides the first consolidated evidence base on humanitarian coordination mechanisms across Africa. In parallel, global benchmarking missions to EU ECHO and the ASEAN AHA Centre generated a reference document capturing lessons on coordination models and governance. These results have already influenced AUC thinking by offering concrete examples of how regional humanitarian agencies structure partnerships, manage surge capacity, and standardize operational tools. The report highlights that these insights are now being used to guide AfHAs establishment phase and will inform collaboration modalities with Member States and regional agencies.
